description.narrative: Stöd till MEM med capacitet höjande projekt för planering och management av energi sektor i Tanzania
Support to MEM capacity for planning and management of the energy sector in Tanzania

The main objective of the support is increased access to modern energy services through enhanced availability, reliability and affordability of energy supplies that are friendly to the environment. It is MEMs role to manage the energy sector through policy design, legislation and regulation supported by channeling of public financial resources to achieve that objective for the benefit of all Tanzanians. The project is a capacity building project that will support Ministry of Energy to better manage the energy sector.
For the Ministry of Energy (MoE) to have quality and reliable data and information, an Energy Information Management System (EIMS) is required. A strong Energy Information Management System requires institutional coordination among different parties in the energy sector as well as proper funding for a sustained capacity building of skilled people with relevant statistical and analytical tools to create and correlate the data at national level.
The main objective of Sida is to assist the Ministry of Energy (MoE) to create an elaborative energy information management system for all types of energy produced and consumed in Tanzania and to harmonize the data available in the region. This should be able to facilitate rapid transfer and exchange of information among regional countries. The Energy Information Management System is expected to be a bedrock of preparation of periodic National Energy Balances; Energy Demand Forecasting as well as Energy Supply Forecasting.

description.narrative:
Based on the Final Project Report, the National Energy Information Management System (NEIMS) was a key component of the Energy Sector Management Capacity Strengthening Project, aimed at strengthening the Governments capacity to collect, manage, analyze and disseminate reliable energy sector information for planning and decision making. The system was designed to address the fragmentation of energy data and provide a more coordinated national platform for energy information management. Tanzanians earlier energy sector reviews had identified the need for a central and shared source of information to support planning and coordination.
The key results can be summarized as follows:
Development of a national energy information management platform: The project supported the development of NEIMS as a centralised platform for collecting, storing, managing and accessing energy sector data. The system is intended to consolidate information from different energy subsectors and institutions and provide a common information base for the Ministry of Energy and other stakeholders.
Improved availability and accessibility of energy sector data: NEIMS established a foundation for improving access to structured and standardised information on energy resources, infrastructure, production, consumption and other sector indicators. This is expected to reduce reliance on fragmented institutional databases and facilitate access to information for planning and analysis.
Strengthened evidence based energy planning and decision making: By bringing energy sector information together in one system, NEIMS is intended to improve the Ministry's ability to analyse trends, identify gaps, monitor sector performance and make evidence based policy and investment decisions.
Improved coordination and information sharing among energy institutions: The system provides a mechanism for strengthening information sharing between the Ministry of Energy and relevant sector institutions. This is particularly important in a sector involving multiple actors, including regulators, utilities, Rural Energy Agency (REA), development institutions and private sector stakeholders.
Enhanced monitoring of energy infrastructure and projects: NEIMS provides a foundation for monitoring energy projects and infrastructure across their lifecycle from projects that are planned or under preparation to those under construction and operational. Recent government audit work confirms that the Ministry developed NEIMS with the objective of consolidating information on renewable energy projects across these different stages.
Improved transparency and public access to energy information: The system includes functionality intended to facilitate public access to energy sector information and analytical outputs. This can contribute to greater transparency and improve the availability of information for investors, researchers, development partners and other stakeholders. The current NEIMS platform describes public data access, interactive charts and downloadable reports as key features.
Strengthened institutional capacity in energy information management: The component contributed to strengthening technical capacity within the Ministry and relevant institutions in data management, analysis and use of information systems. This is an important institutional result because the sustainability of NEIMS depends not only on the technology but also on the capacity of staff to maintain, update and use the system.
Foundation for improved sector monitoring and reporting: NEIMS provides an important basis for establishing more systematic and timely reporting on energy sector performance. It can support monitoring of national energy targets, investment programmes, renewable energy development, energy consumption and other key indicators.
Energy sector project monitoring and coordination strengthened NEIMS provides a foundation for consolidating information on energy projects and tracking them across different stages of implementation. This can strengthen coordination, improve monitoring of project progress and help reduce duplication, particularly for renewable energy initiatives.
Transparency and accessibility of energy information enhanced The NEIMS platform provides functionality for public access to selected energy information, including interactive charts and downloadable reports and datasets, creating a stronger basis for transparency and informed stakeholder engagement.
Evidence base for energy policy, planning and investment decisions strengthened By integrating harmonized energy data with reporting, analysis and forecasting functions, NEIMS provides an important foundation for more evidence based policy formulation, strategic planning and investment decisions. This aligns with the Ministry's broader mandate for energy policy, planning and resource management.
Project completed successfully despite implementation delays and risks Although stakeholder availability, iterative reviews and approval processes resulted in schedule adjustments, all planned outputs were ultimately completed without reducing the project scope or quality. The system transitioned to the operational phase, with 95% of the contract value paid and 5% retained during the Defect Liability Period.
